column1: # Only REVIEW findings can be acknowledged here. A FATAL finding cannot: it is
# either a lockfile that cannot be trusted, or a demonstrable closure loss, and
# silencing it is exactly how a green gate hides a dead workflow.
# Every row is a claim that a human looked at this defect and decided it is not
# to be fixed in this change. Remove a row as soon as the defect is fixed; a row
# that matches no current finding is reported as NOT RUN (BASELINE-STALE), so an
# acknowledgement cannot outlive its subject unnoticed.
# fields: rule <TAB> subject <TAB> reason <TAB> reviewer <TAB> date

column3: Two immutable snapshots are recorded for one moved ref (v1). The 02cb… record backs panicbot-sweep.yml's inline @v1; the e2a5… record backs the standards mirror reusable at 75bd. Re-resolving either without the other's owner is a silent behaviour change, so it needs a reviewed re-pin, not an audit-time rewrite.

dogfood-gate.yml pins the validate-action subpath at @main. The lock records an immutable snapshot, but the ref itself is not an immutable pin. Fixing it means changing the dogfood-gate caller (and possibly the action's release tags), which is outside a lock-closure change.
Same class as deed-ecosystem@main: dogfood-gate.yml pins the validate-action subpath at @main while the lock freezes a snapshot. Needs a reviewed tag on the action, not an audit-time rewrite.
